chains.title: E2F4 binds the alt allele more strongly and, if repressive here, lowers POU5F1B

links.claim: QBiC-SELEX group G018 contains an own model for E2F4 that passes with the same sign as the best E2F1 model (E2F4 z 10.46; predicted_effect > 0), so the alt C allele is predicted to bind E2F4 more strongly. E2F4 is the highest-expressed covered E2F in the HCT116 DepMap context (134.92 TPM), which is why I select E2F4 within the shared E2F specificity rather than the best-model E2F1.
The variant lies in cCRE EH38E3858447, a proximal enhancer-like element with DNase and H3K27ac signal, and VEP annotates an ENSR8_CGMBX enhancer at this site.

POU5F1B is the strongest L2G gene (0.83) in the credible sets containing this position and is among the cCRE-nearby genes; however those credible sets are for PSA and urinary incontinence, not colorectal cancer, and no colon transverse eQTL is reported, so the target-gene link is indirect.
HCT116 is the DepMap expression context and expresses E2F4 at 134.92 TPM; the enhancer annotation is ENCODE biosample-maximum, not HCT116-specific, so activity in HCT116 is plausible but unproven.

POU5F1B has literature support in colon cancer growth, invasion and angiogenesis, but CRISPR dependency in HCT116 and bowel lineage is minimal, and E2F4 repressor activity at this enhancer is not shown; the proposed direction is therefore conditional.

predictions: Recombinant E2F4-DP1 binds the alt oligo more strongly than ref.
Allele-specific E2F4 ChIP in HCT116 shows higher alt-allele occupancy.
If E2F4 represses this element, the alt allele lowers reporter activity and POU5F1B allelic expression.
falsified_if: Recombinant E2F4-DP1 binds ref equal to or more strongly than alt.
Allele-specific E2F4 ChIP in HCT116 shows no alt-allele occupancy preference.
The alt allele does not lower POU5F1B or reporter activity in an E2F4-dependent assay.

checks.why: Tests whether rs73706717 is a molecular eQTL for POU5F1B or MYC in colon, directly strengthening or weakening the target-gene link that currently relies on non-colorectal L2G evidence.
Checks whether E2F4 actually occupies this element in HCT116; absence of a peak would strongly undercut the QBiC-SELEX-only E2F4 binding claim.
Tests whether POU5F1B is a colorectal-cancer-relevant dependency, addressing the phenotype link and the relevance of the proposed target gene.
